_comment: Correctness sweep: every (rows x cols) cell is run once per entry in
qt_param_sets, so the two implementations are compared across the cases where
they could disagree about WHAT the answer is rather than how fast they get
there. measure_time is false, so the grid stays small and the file finishes in
a couple of minutes. Each set carries its own n_jobs; there is no top-level
n_jobs axis here, because threading is one of the things under test rather
than a dimension to sweep.
Both implementations receive the SAME float64 array (the native kernel and
np.nanpercentile both work in float64) and the same random_state, so when
subsample is active they resample identical rows. Any difference in the CSV
is therefore a real difference in arithmetic, not in inputs. The CSV reports
those differences as MAE and max |delta|, not as a pass/fail against a
tolerance: what is being measured is float64 round-off, a few ulps, and the
number itself is the result.
What each set is for. The adapter overrides exactly two hooks -- _dense_fit
(native kernel) and _transform (NumPy rewrite + n_jobs fan-out) -- and the
rewrite is only partial: uniform output still runs scikit-learn's own
_transform_col, while normal output runs the custom _transform_col_normal.
1. baseline        - uniform, serial, clean data. The reference point: only
the native fit differs from scikit-learn here, so a
mismatch is a plain kernel bug rather than an
interaction. It has to be measured first.
2. normal_parallel - the most-rewritten path and the threading, together.
_transform_col_normal replaces stats.norm.ppf/cdf with
the ndtri/ndtr ufuncs, hoists the reversed/negated
quantile arrays out of the per-feature loop, and clips
with module-level constants; n_jobs 8 adds the
Fortran-order copy and the ThreadPoolExecutor branch on
top. Both are claimed to be value-for-value identities,
so folding them into one set loses no attribution: if
this disagrees and set 1 does not, the rewrite is where
to look.
3. ragged          - the compound data-shape set. 10 % NaN exercises the
kernel's NaN-dropping column gather and the masked
gather/scatter branch of _transform_col_normal (the
all-finite fast path skips it everywhere else), and
transform_nan_agree proves NaNs come out where they went
in. One all-NaN column adds the kernel's early-return
branch, the one place it produces a value without
sorting anything. Integer levels add ties, so order
statistics coincide and quantiles_ repeats values --
this is what catches interpolation that is only
algebraically right, since on tied neighbours a
weighted-sum lerp rounds an ulp off the sample and makes
quantiles_ non-monotonic, which np.interp's xp contract
forbids. Watch the monotonic columns here. n_quantiles
1000 against 160 fit rows in the smallest cell also
triggers scikit-learn's n_quantiles > n_samples clipping
in the inherited fit.
4. subsample_active - subsample 128, below the fit rows of every cell, so
resample actually runs. The only set that checks the
adapter draws the SAME subsample as scikit-learn: it
reimplements _dense_fit, so it also reimplements the
resample call, and consuming the rng differently would
fit different data while still looking plausible.
Dropped axes and why. dtype is not swept: float32 input makes the kernel
decline and the adapter fall back to scikit-learn's own _dense_fit, so the
cell would compare scikit-learn against itself. That path is a warning
contract, not an arithmetic one, and it is covered by
stratum/tests/adapters/test_quantile_transformer.py. copy is not swept: it
changes whether the input buffer is reused, not what is computed. Sparse input
is not swept: the native kernel backs _dense_fit only, so a sparse matrix runs
scikit-learn's inherited _sparse_fit unchanged and there is nothing of ours
left to compare. inverse_transform is not a set of its own -- every cell
already inverts, and it is fed the SAME transformed matrix for both
implementations so the inverse columns isolate the inverse path instead of
compounding the forward difference.

qt_param_sets._axis: reference point; uniform output, serial transform, clean data
qt_param_sets.name: baseline

qt_param_sets._axis: data: NaNs + an all-NaN column + ties; and n_quantiles above the fit rows
qt_param_sets.name: ragged

qt_param_sets._axis: subsample: null -> 128; both must resample the SAME rows
qt_param_sets.name: subsample_active
